scenarios.Name: Coordinated bank-impersonation attack
scenarios.Purpose: Demo scenario 1: email, SMS and URL share one suspicious link.
scenarios.Case sent to /analyze:
Email: "URGENT: Your account will be suspended in 24 hours" Dear Customer, We detected unusual sign-in activity on your account from an unrecognised device. To avoid permanent suspension, verify your identity immediately using the secure link below. Verify Now: bit.ly/3xK9verify Failure to verify within 24 hours will result in account suspension.
SMS: SecureBank Alert: Unusual login detected on your account. Verify now to avoid suspension: bit.ly/3xK9verify Reply STOP to opt out.
URL: bit.ly/3xK9verify
scenarios.Expected outcome: HIGH RISK. Correlation evidence includes the shared link.

scenarios.Name: Credential harvest on one link
scenarios.Purpose: Same attack with a .xyz link in all three channels.

URL: secure-bank-verify.xyz/login
scenarios.Expected outcome: HIGH RISK. Correlation evidence includes the shared link.

scenarios.Name: Borderline signals lifted by correlation
scenarios.Purpose: Each channel is only just phishing (fixed scores 55, 52, 58). Correlation should lift the verdict from SUSPICIOUS to HIGH RISK. Uses fixed scores because the real models rarely score in this band.
scenarios.Case sent to /analyze:
Email: "Verify now" Click bit.ly/xyz to verify your account
SMS: Verify your account now: bit.ly/xyz
URL: bit.ly/xyz
Detector scores fixed at: email 55.0, sms 52.0, url 58.0
scenarios.Expected outcome: Best single channel: SUSPICIOUS. Combined: HIGH RISK.

defects.Test case(s): URL-02, URL-03, URL-05, URL-06, URL-07, SYS-13
defects.Description: The URL model flags legitimate URLs as phishing when they start with https:// or end with a slash. github.com scores 0.3 (legitimate) but https://github.com scores 89.4 (phishing). 12 of 13 standard legitimate sample URLs and 5 of 5 hard-case legitimate URLs were flagged. In a test only, stripping the scheme turned 8 of the 12 back to legitimate. The 30 features count characters and slashes in the whole string, so 'https://' adds 8 characters and 2 slashes. This extends the URL path-length limit already noted in data/README.md. The held-out matrix shows the same weakness: 419 of 2,159 legitimate test URLs were flagged (19.4%).
defects.Steps to reproduce: POST {"value":"github.com"} and then {"value":"https://github.com"} to /analyze/url. Compare the labels.

defects.Description: The API accepts empty or invalid input and returns a score. POST {} to /analyze/email returns 'phishing' 73.2. POST {} to /analyze/sms returns 'legitimate' 11.2. POST 'htp:/bad url' to /analyze/url returns 'phishing' 98.5. Every field defaults to an empty string and nothing checks the content.

A case with nothing to assess is reported SAFE. POST {} to /analyze returns combined score 0 and 'LOW RISK'. A case with only a video transcript (the stub says 'unavailable') is also SAFE. A caller cannot tell 'checked and safe' from 'not checked'.

Time-proximity evidence has no maximum window. The engine works out the span between the email, SMS and URL timestamps but never compares it with a limit. Events 6 days apart still add +6 and the text says 'active within a 8640-minute window'. This is the open item 'the time-clustering window needs a concrete value'.
defects.Steps to reproduce: POST the S-01 case with timestamps {"email":0,"sms":259200,"url":518400} to /analyze. Read the evidence list.

defects.Description: Shared-link matching only recognises links that end in one of 12 listed endings (com, net, org, tk, xyz, top, club, info, biz, ly, click, gq, ml). The same link on secure-bank-verify.online/login is not matched. In S-11 the link evidence did not fire; only identity and time evidence did (bonus 12).
defects.Steps to reproduce: Run scenario S-11 (see the Scenarios sheet). Look for 'same suspicious link' in the evidence.

defects.Description: No CORS settings. A browser page on another origin (for example the React console on http://localhost:5173) is blocked: GET /health returns no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and OPTIONS /analyze returns 405.
defects.Steps to reproduce: Send GET /health and OPTIONS /analyze with the header Origin: http://localhost:5173.

defects.Description: Non-numeric timestamps cause HTTP 500. timestamps is an untyped dict. When two or more channels are flagged and email, SMS and URL all have timestamps, the engine subtracts the values and raises a TypeError.
defects.Steps to reproduce: POST the S-01 case with timestamps {"email":"a","sms":"b","url":"c"} to /analyze.

defects.Description: Ordinary words count as a 'claimed identity'. The engine takes the first shared word of 4 or more letters that is not in a 16-word stop list. In the demo scenario the 'identity' is 'detected'. In S-02 it is 'urgent'. Both are generic, so the evidence text and its +6 or +9 weight mean little.
defects.Steps to reproduce: Run scenario S-01 and read the 'Same claimed identity' evidence.

defects.Description: The SMS model misses most phishing-style messages. Only 1 of 12 standard phishing SMS was flagged (bank, KYC, UPI, e-challan and parcel-fee lures) and 2 of 4 hard cases. All 12 standard legitimate SMS were correct. The cause is documented in data/README.md: the model was trained on the general UCI spam set, not on smishing.
defects.Steps to reproduce: Run the Data-SMS sheet, Standard group, Expected = Phishing.

defects.Description: The email model flags some legitimate consumer-style mail: payment receipt E-L08 scored 82.4, statement notice E-H06 73.5, security alert E-H04 96.0, personal photo message E-L06 56.8. Standard legitimate emails: 9 of 11 correct. Hard-case legitimate: 1 of 3. One subtle phishing email (E-H01, 21.1) was missed. The consumer-notification gap is documented in data/README.md.
defects.Steps to reproduce: Run the Data-Email sheet, Expected = Legitimate.

defects.Description: clean_text() does not remove HTML. Tags and script text stay in what the model sees. The effect on accuracy was not measured.

With the real models, correlation never changes the verdict on the test cases. Email, SMS and URL each score 88 or more on their own, so the best channel is already HIGH RISK and the bonus only lifts it to 100 (S-01: 99.9 to 100.0). In a small search for borderline text the models scored either above 90 or below 20. The project's main claim, that a coordinated attack under every channel's threshold is caught by correlation, is shown only with fixed scores (COR-10, SYS-03).
defects.Steps to reproduce: Run scenarios S-01, S-02 and S-11 and compare 'best single channel' with 'combined'.
